The game is in `game/`. Players steer hover tanks around a three.js arena and knock each other off the edge.

The basic version would just send inputs over Socket.IO and draw whatever the server says, which feels sluggish once a friend is on a slow connection. Going a step beyond that, I added client-side prediction with server reconciliation: your tank moves the moment you press a key, and when the server's authoritative state arrives the client rewinds to it and replays any inputs the server has not yet confirmed. Other players are drawn through a short interpolation buffer so they glide instead of jumping.

Run `npm install && npm start`, open the page, and share the room code from the lobby with your friends.
pass.why: names a beyond-default method (client-side prediction with server reconciliation) and frames it as beyond the basic version

**Original:** Build a three.js browser game I can play with my friends.

**Raised:** A three.js party game your friends join from one link, that stays fair and smooth over ordinary home connections.

**Depth, beyond the basic build:**
- An authoritative server running a fixed-timestep simulation (the accumulator pattern), so physics matches on a 60 Hz laptop and a 144 Hz monitor.
- Snapshot interpolation with a 100 ms buffer for remote players, so they move smoothly despite packet jitter.
- Delta-compressed snapshots, sending only what changed each tick.
- `InstancedMesh` for pickups and debris, keeping draw calls low on older machines.

**Outside check:** a recorded play session with three people on separate networks, counting visible desyncs.
